newsitem.title: MEXICO: Coparmex sees Mexican economic recovery in Q2 1997.
newsitem.headline: Coparmex sees Mexican economic recovery in Q2 1997.

text.p: The leader of the Mexican Employers Confederation (Coparmex) said Monday that a general economic recovery would be felt by virtually all Mexican businesses during the second quarter of next year.

"For the second quarter of 1997, we expect general economic reactivation," Carlos Abascal Carranza, president of Coparmex, told Reuters in an interview. "The construction industry and other related sectors, retailers and services need to have a vision that the country will enter a general reactivation."
The construction sector, which shrank by more than 20 percent, was among the most affected by the economic crisis resulting from the December 1994 peso devaluation.

"Controlling inflation has benefited interest rates above all and will result in a profound reactivation of internal credit in 1997," Abascal said. Coparmex predicted economic growth of about five percent for 1997, with inflation of about 15 percent, he said.

Abascal also urged the government to rewrite tax laws in order to promote the private sector. "If we are to be the motor of the economy, we want adequate conditions in order to play this role," he said. "Fiscal laws should not be just about collecting taxes, but rather promoting economic activity."
